summary: This article explains how neurons connect and grow stronger paths when we practice, and how mistakes, sleep, smart study habits, and healthy living help the brain learn.
introduce: Drop a pencil and ask, “What was the cause? What was the effect?” to model the idea quickly. Then show the title “How Your Brain Learns” and tell students to look for things in the article that make other things happen.

keyTerms.def: a link that joins two or more things
a small, curved part of the brain that helps make new memories

challengeTerms.def: the brain's ability to change and build new connections throughout life
the tiny gap where one nerve cell passes a signal to another
to make something stronger and more lasting by bringing it together

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that making mistakes is a good way to learn? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Write advice for a younger student who wants to learn better.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review connection, strengthen, and hippocampus, and let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses neuroplasticity, synapse, and consolidate to explain one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
